chunks: And from him, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, all from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the woman who performs Khul'a (compensatory divorce). He said: It is not permissible for her husband to divorce her by Khul'a until she says: 'I shall not fulfill a vow for you, nor establish the limits of Allah with regard to you, nor wash myself for you from major impurity, and I will surely settle on your bed, and I will let into your house the one whom you dislike, without you knowing this, and they will not speak to her, and she is the one who says this.' So when she performs Khul'a, she is irrevocably divorced, and for him is that he takes from her wealth whatever he is able to, and it is not for him that he takes from the woman who disavows (the marriage) everything which he had given her.

key_terms.الْمُبَارِئَةِ: The woman who disavows (refers to the wife in Khul'a context)
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةِ: The woman who performs Khul'a (compensatory divorce)
key_terms.يَخْلَعَهَا: To divorce by Khul'a (unfastening the marriage bond)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific verbal conditions and financial rulings for Khul'a in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the precise verbal formula a wife must recite to initiate Khul'a, emphasizing the husband's right to retain the initial dowry (mahr) while exempting him from returning additional gifts. It highlights the irrevocable nature of the divorce ('bain') once the condition is met, reflecting the Shia juristic view that Khul'a is a contractual dissolution where the wife buys her freedom from the marriage bond.
